data.reasoning: Report 2 (deepseek) successfully reviewed all three files and found the package safe. The PKGBUILD uses standard AUR patterns: VCS source with pinned tag (v1.1.0), SKIP checksum (standard for VCS sources), and installs from the project's own GitHub repository. Report 1's inconclusive result was caused by API failures (HTTP 400 errors) during the full file review phase, not by genuine security concerns. Notably, Report 1's initial PKGBUILD audit succeeded and also found it safe. Both successful reviews agree the package is safe.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement is not substantive - it's caused by tool errors in Report 1 (qwen model). The API requests for .SRCINFO and PKGBUILD failed with HTTP 400 BadRequestError during the full file review phase, resulting in an inconclusive verdict. Report 2 (deepseek) completed successfully and found no issues. The initial PKGBUILD audit in Report 1 also succeeded and found it safe, confirming the package is not malicious.
coverage_issues: Report 1 (qwen) failed to review .SRCINFO and PKGBUILD due to API errors (HTTP 400 BadRequestError)
Report 1's full file review was incomplete, though its initial PKGBUILD audit succeeded
learnings: API failures during file review should trigger automatic retry or fallback to initial audit results when available
When initial PKGBUILD audit succeeds but full file review fails due to tool errors, the system should better reconcile these results rather than marking as inconclusive
Tool errors (API failures, timeouts) should be clearly distinguished from genuine security uncertainty in the verdict logic
